Tuning note: Start of the main injection in crank degrees before TDC - higher number = more advance. More advance raises cylinder pressure, power and noise and lowers EGT; too much advance can damage pistons and head gaskets.
The ECU blends the Low / Mid / Sea-level versions of this table by barometric pressure (altitude); edit all three to change behaviour everywhere. Used in normal combustion mode (C1) - the mode the truck runs in almost all the time. This is a air temp correction applied on top of the base table.

Name: Driver Torque Request - Delta Neutral (torque)
FolderName: 11 Driver Demand (Pedal) - Tables and Curves: " "
Comment:
Driver Torque Request - Delta Neutral (torque)
GM name: KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral | table (5 rows x 3 columns) | units: ratio
What it does: This table is used to ramp from the new launch torque to the neutral progression torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. Inputs are the latched delta difference between these two torques at the falling edge of launch active pedal and the time since the falling edge. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is very high, then the likely cause is from overscaled values between launch and normal neutral or pedal progression tables. These large overscaled values can change very quickly and its important to ramp out the delta torque quickly to prevent an (overscaled) drop in either the neutral or pedal torque causing the blended torque to drop suddenly and ramp slowly. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is fairly small, then it is important to ramp slowly until the vehicle speed blending is finished so that there is minimal change in the overall launch torque (fast ramping in this scenario could make the launch torque drop toofast causing the launch to feel slugish). Cal out values are all 100. Default values are: [[0.1, 5, 100][0.5, 5, 100][5, 50, 100][10, 100, 100][512, 512, 512]]
Rows: Torque (KnDTRC_M_DeltaNeutralAxis) (5 points, Nm, 0 to 100) - This calibratable axis uses VeDTRC_DeltaM_NeutralFallEdge to determine which row of KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral should be used to ramp out delta launch torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. The values of this table are signed and represent thelatched value of the difference between launch torque and the normal neutral progression torque (VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod) at the falling edge of launch active pedal becoming CbFALSE. Negative values correspond to launch torques that are higher than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Positive values correspond to launch torques that are lower than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Coolant Temp Input - BH Rebound Delta Max (temperature)
GM name: KeECTI_T_BHReboundDeltaMax | single value | units: deg C
What it does: This cal is for the control block heater detection only. It does not affect any of the ECT sensor diagnostics. After a block heater is used, and then engine is subsequently started, coolant temperature will generally drop temporarely and then startrising again. The control block heater algorithm looks for this dip in the coolant temperature and then looks for the start of rise again. When the risinf of the sensor indicated coolant temperature happens, the blending of the sudo coolant temperature towards the sensor indicated coolant temperature will start. This cal represents how much does the sensor indicated coolant temperature has to rise again after dropping before the blending would start. This cal should be set to abput two degrees,not too much higher to identify the start of the rise quickly, and not too much lower to avoid misidentification of the start of the rise due to noise in the coolant temperature signal.

GM name: KtECTI_pct_BHSensedMinPosition | table (17 rows x 4 columns) | units: %
What it does: This cal is for the control block heater detection only. It does not affect any of the ECT sensor diagnostics. The percent offset between the coolant temperature indicated by the coolant sensor and the intake air temperature at power-up. A 10% valuewould place the coolant temperature at IAT + 10% of the difference between the indicated coolant temperature and IAT. A 100% value would set this coolant temperature at the indicated coolant temperature. This cal is indexed for different zones on the engine block, and is also a function of the difference between the indicated coolant temperature and IAT at powerup. This offset calculated at powerup is carried on and removed from the indicated coolant temperature as the engine runs, until the thermostat open temperature is reached or until a dip in the coolant temperature occurs.
Rows: Temperature (KnECTI_T_PositionDeltaTAxis) (17 points, deg C, 0 to 100) - This cal is for the control block heater detection only. It does not affect any of the ECT sensor diagnostics. This is the placement between IAT and sensed coolant used in KaECTI_pct_BHSensedMinPosition. The difference between ECT and IAT at power-up (or ECT and EOT if available and chosen to be used) is used as input against this axis to lookup the proper percentage between ECT and IAT (or ECT and EOT if available and chosen to be used). This would consitute the corrected (or sudo) coolant temperature.

This is the index axis to be used in KaECTI_pct_BHSensedMinPosition. The global sudo coolant temperature will use only one index or columnin this table. Other locations on the engine block that need more specific correction to the sensed coolant temperature will use a different index in this axis, and fill in their desired correction in KaECTI_pct_BHSensedMinPosition corresponding totheir index.

What it does: This calibration is used toselectively enable reporting of Vref Supply DTCs for differentcontrollers. A maximum of five DTCs can be selected to reportout of seven available for a controller. These DTCs are C0880,C0890, P0641, P0651, P0697, P06A3, P06D2 and can be enabled byCiVLTI_i_UserGainSwRefVoltCkt, CiVLTI_i_ManApplySwRefVoltCkt,CiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt1Ckt, CiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt2Ckt,CiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt3Ckt,CiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt4Ckt, andCiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt5Ckt respectively. The order of selectionshould be taken care on some controllers, particularly PTcontrollers, such that right DTCs get enabled for a fault. Forexample: P0641 maps to CiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt1Ckt, P0651 maps toCiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt2Ckt, P0697 maps toCiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt2Ckt andP06A3 maps toCiVLTI_i_SnsrRefVolt4Ckt. For Chassis controllersCiVLTI_i_UserGainSwRefVoltCkt and CiVLTI_i_ManApplySwRefVoltCktcan be selected to report C0880 and C0890 respectively. Hereorder of selection may or may not be important.

Comment:
Engine Position Input - Cam Edge Raw Learn Delay (time)
GM name: KeEPSI_t_CamEdgeRawLrnDly | single value | units: s
What it does: Minimum time between successful learn sequences. The learn sequence may run continuously while the engine is in sync and phasers are parked (and no faults exist). To reduce throughput and risk of corrupting learned NVM values, a delay is applied from the time a learn is completed until the time a new learn it started. However, there isnt any delay if a learn sequence is disabled or aborted prior to completing. For example, if a learn sequence encounters too many invalid cam edges (out-of-rangevalues), then the learn is disabled and a new learn is re-started as soon as conditions allow (without any delay).
